packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-06 -- unverified image reading (blind first reader)

Exposure statement: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or reading of this fragment. I listed the packet directory (file names and sizes only) and read pixel dimensions with sips to tell overviews from tiles; packet.json was not opened.

LAYOUT SURVEY

Face A (overview image-001.jpg; tiles image-002..016, apparently 5 columns x 3 rows):
- Parchment bifolium/wrapper photographed open, landscape, with a vertical fold/spine roughly 45% from the right edge (where small holes/sewing stations are visible). It has been reused as a cover for a later paper volume.
- Right panel (front cover of the reuse): later German title in large Fraktur/Kanzlei script, in dark ink, 6 lines plus a word:
  "Gotshaus Stambs / Oberkellner Ambts / Vrbar, auf das 94 / Jar, sambt den 93 / vnd Elltern Jars / Resstanntten" (read from the overview; see tile readings). Also a round paper label with "IV" (?) at top left of that panel, a pencil/blue-crayon number "N. 140" (?) further down, a violet stamp "Stiftsarchiv Stams" with an underline, and a small pencil shelfmark at bottom right ("Stams, Stift, Frag. 135"?).
- Left panel: surface very worn and stained; vertical ruling lines (bounding lines for a column or columns) visible; a few faint traces of writing along the left edge, rotated 90 degrees (a vertical line of script near x~370). No legible medieval text visible at overview scale on this face; the earlier text, if present, is on the other face or abraded.
- Interpretation (tentative): this face is the outside of a reused medieval leaf/bifolium, with the original text on the inside face.

Face B (overview image-017.jpg; tiles image-018..029, apparently 4 columns x 3 rows):
- Same sheet, other side, landscape; the fold runs vertically at about x~930 of the overview. Text is written in long lines straight across the whole width, crossing the fold: i.e. the original was a single-sheet document (charter-like layout), later folded as a wrapper. No columns.
- Language/script observation: German vernacular in a late-medieval/early-modern cursive (Kanzlei/Kurrent-type) hand, brown ink. No rubrics, no enlarged initials seen, no glosses.
- Upper ~half heavily faded/abraded (only scattered words); text becomes legible from about overview y~600 down to the bottom edge (y~960), about 14-15 lines. Left margin strip (x~150-350) is folded/creased and partly cut off; line beginnings at the left are lost or very faint. Right edge of lines is near the trimmed edge.
- Bottom edge: last line partly cut by the trim (descenders/lower half lost in places). A pencil shelfmark "Stams, Stift, Frag. 135" (?) top left. Stains at upper right.
- Plan: read the lower legible block first (bottom tile row 026-029, then middle row 022-025), then the faded upper row 018-021, then Face A tiles as the image budget permits.

TILE ORDER NOTE (Face B): the tile numbers run in a grid rotated 180 degrees relative to the overview, while the tile images themselves are upright. image-026 shows the upper-right corner (round orange stain) and image-018 the lower-right corner of the written block. So: row 018-021 = bottom strip of the face, from right (018) to left (021); 022-025 = middle strip, right to left; 026-029 = top strip, right to left. (Inferred from two tiles; the rest checked as I go.)

image-026.jpg (Face B, upper-right corner; read before the order was understood): faint, abraded writing only; the visible strokes look disconnected (heavy, partly offset/show-through-like). Fragments seen, none confidently legible: line ~5 "..vor .. [illegible]"; line ~9 "..Morimmy?.."; line ~11 "..Bey? .. vnd? .."; I cannot read connected text here at this resolution. Large orange round stain and smaller blotches at left; fold crease across the top.

image-018.jpg (Face B, lower-right corner; right ends of the last 12 lines). Line 1 is cut at the top of the tile; left edge cut mid-word throughout.
018.01 [...]n? [illegible] zu? freyung? , [illegible]rungen?   (top half of letters cut)
018.02 [...]wed?er mit noch on Recht. noch sunst
018.03 [...]ch hinach?ssen? wie vor. sollicher seiner
018.04 [...]r vnns vnd vnnser Erben genntzlichen
018.05 [...]schafft Tyrol on allen vorbehallt.
018.06 [...]geben wellen. Aller getreulich vnnd
018.07 [...]t vnd sonnderlichen für vnns vnd vnser
018.08 [...] Petersperg. Das er von Gerichtsharr?n? .   (the word before the stop is uncertain: Gerichts-h..)

018.10 [...]? Erbern Hanns Jörg? Sturm diser?zeit

018.12 [...] [illegible]hundert? vnnd zwaintzigisten Jar.   (lower parts cut by the trimmed edge; "zwaintzigisten Jar" fairly clear)
Notes: in line 018.05 "schafft" has a strong crossed double-f ligature; superscript marks over u (ü/ů) in "für", "Jörg"(?).

image-019.jpg (Face B, bottom strip, centre-right; same 12 lines as 018, continuing leftward; the fold runs vertically through x~750 of the tile, with small holes). Line numbers match 018's (019.n continues into 018.n).

019.04 [...]rechtigkaiten genntz? vnd ewigklichen für vnns vn[d]

019.12 [...]li?macher? [illegible]h?ü?[illegible] [illegible] [ ? ]hundert? Zwain?[...]   (lower half cut by trim; very uncertain)
Notes: "Sylz?" -- the first letter is a long descender stroke with a loop; could be S or V; second letter y/g. "Phleger" has a ph- ligature. "Wirtlewt" could be "Wirtleut"; I see w-like form. "sament" may carry a stroke I cannot see.

Notes: "Gotzhaus" reads "Gotzhaws"/"Gotshauß"-like; "Conuent" with u. "Ca?ssle?" is a surname with long-s ligature, possibly "Casse" or "Cassle". "Belsch" vs "Welsch": initial looks like a W/B with loop.

Aller getreulich vnnd" -- correction: 020.06 begins "[...] dem" which overlaps 021's "durch dem"; the word after "dem" on 021 begins "Abb"/"Gotz"? -- ambiguous where 021 and 020 overlap; I read "Abb" on 021 and "Gotzhaus?" on 020, one of which is wrong, or these are two different words ("dem Abbt ... dem Gotzhaus"). - All 29 images viewed (2 overviews, 27 tiles); no image was removed from view during the session, so no hand-off file was written.
- Face A ("135r" by the pencil shelfmark) carries no medieval text that I can see: only the later cover title "Gotßhaus Stambs / Oberkellner Ambts / Vrbar, auf das 94 / Jar, sambt den 93 / vnd Elltern Jars / Resstannten", an "IV/18" label, "Hs. 140", the "Stiftsarchiv Stams" stamp, and one faint vertical dorsal-type note at the left edge (image-002) that I could not read.

Essentially unread: the upper half of Face B (tiles 026-029 and upper parts of 022-025) and the left ~third of every line (tiles 021, 025, 029), which are abraded to ghost strokes. The date line (L12) is cut by the bottom trim; the year's hundreds are not legible.
